correctness.rationale: The Stieltjes representation on (0,1] includes the possible pointwise endpoint jump and has total variation equal to the input seminorm. Bernstein reproduces constants, so the L² triangle inequality bounds the norm by the supremum of single-jump errors; the unit-variation steps prove the converse. Within each cell the sampled threshold is fixed and d(E²)/dt=2F−1, an increasing function, yielding the two traces per grid point. The artificial endpoint traces (0,0) and (n,n+1) are zero, the right trace (0,1) is a limit, and (n,n) is attained. Reconstructed 270 traces exactly in the Bernstein basis (product coefficients followed by an antiderivative of degree 2n+1), replay `python /workspace/review_checks/4.py`. For n≤14 the only largest trace labels are (0,1) and (n,n), of value 1/(2n+1); for n=15 only (6,7) and (9,9) give 7885956840965217/239784545898437500, strictly above 1/31. The latter trace is the admissible step at 3/5. A separate reviewer-written replay via beta integration agreed. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed. For interior t_n→t, the binomial CLT with bounded third moments and variance comparable to n gives pointwise Φ(z) at x=t_n+sqrt(t_n(1−t_n)/n)z; Hoeffding outside the bounded scaled neighborhood gives an integrable Gaussian majorant uniformly for t_n in compact interior ranges, including shifted thresholds. Writing Q=1−Φ, integration by parts gives ∫₀∞Q²=φ(0)−2∫₀∞φ²=(sqrt(2)−1)/(2sqrt(π)). For the frozen Chebyshev justification of (7), the threshold n|x−t|−1 has to be positive, not merely its squared denominator; the splitting uses Chebyshev only there and the bound 1 in the near part. An independent check is to write F as the CDF of the jth order statistic U of n uniform variables. Jensen gives ∫(F−1_{x≥t})²≤E|U−t|. Its beta mean is m=j/(n+1), variance m(1−m)/(n+2); |m−t|≤2/n implies (7), also for the limiting traces j∈[1,n], and both omitted constant-threshold endpoints are zero. Compactness now excludes both endpoints at scale √n and maximizes sqrt(t(1−t)) uniquely at t=1/2. This proves the displayed sharp asymptotic and the location conclusion, not a finite-n optimizer classification beyond 15.

evidence: Berry–Esseen and the binomial expectation can justify a local layer, but worst-case integrated squared loss requires uniform boundary control and exact finite optimization. An exact L¹ norm does not give the squared integrals: even for a single jump, squaring before integration changes the values, and the bound by the L¹ error for a unit step is not sharp in general.

value.rationale: The jump model and endpoint convention are intrinsic to point sampling on Jordan BV. The exact transition distinguishes the endpoint artifact from a genuine interior extremizer, and the large-degree sharp constant plus localization resolve which jump configurations govern worst squared error. The cutoff is a structural fact for a classical operator, not an arbitrary isolated computation.
